characters.summary: Vision fights using density manipulation to phase through attacks or become diamond-hard, alongside energy projection from the Mind Stone on his forehead and native flight. He possesses superhuman strength, durability, and a synthetic body that can calculate complex data instantly.
weaknesses: Corvus Glaive's blade disrupting density powers
limitations: Power source is entirely dependent on the Mind Stone
Severely weakened when ambushed and stabbed by Corvus Glaive

sources.supports: General abilities, Vibranium body, Mind Stone, and phasing powers in MCU.
Specific combat techniques, density manipulation, and vulnerabilities against Corvus Glaive.

feats.claim: Fires a concentrated energy beam from the Mind Stone on his forehead.

notableResults.note: Vision easily restrains Hawkeye during the airport battle.
Vision is ambushed in Edinburgh and incapacitated by Corvus Glaive's special blade.

campaignTags.claim: Vision flies naturally using his internal mechanics and Mind Stone connection.
Vision is a synthetic android created by Ultron and JARVIS.

unknowns: Exact limits of his vibranium density changes against cosmic-level attacks.

characters.summary: Adrian Toomes uses an advanced mechanical flight suit equipped with articulated mechanical wings, projectile weapons, and sharp talon-like feet. He relies on aerial mobility, stealth in dark environments, and high-speed dive attacks.

mechanisms: Helmet with HUD and environmental protection

weaknesses: Suit is vulnerable to structural overload and explosive combustion of Chitauri power cores
limitations: Power source relies on volatile Chitauri energy cores that can detonate under damage

sources.supports: Adrian Toomes, Vulture suit capabilities, Chitauri tech, and combat style in Spider-Man: Homecoming.

feats.claim: Hijacks a Stark cargo plane mid-air using his flight harness and specialized cutting equipment.

notableResults.note: Vulture collapses a building roof on Spider-Man, nearly killing him.
Vulture's suit malfunctions and explodes during a fight on a cargo plane, leading to his arrest.

campaignTags.claim: Vulture flies using a mechanical wing harness powered by Chitauri energy cores.
Suit is built from salvaged Chitauri and Stark Industries technology.

unknowns: Exact durability of the wings against continuous heavy artillery.

characters.summary: James Rhodes uses heavily armored military-grade exoskeleton suits loaded with conventional ballistic weaponry, missiles, and shoulder-mounted cannons. He fights as a flying heavy gunner utilizing overwhelming firepower and sustained flight.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to high-voltage energy attacks that can short-circuit suit systems
limitations: Limited ammunition reserves requiring reloading or resupply

sources.supports: James Rhodes, War Machine suit iterations, heavy weaponry, and MCU history.
Mark IV armor specifications and heavy ordnance.

feats.claim: Decimates a swarm of Outriders using heavy carpet bombing and shoulder turrets.

notableResults.note: Rhodes is accidentally shot down by Vision while engaging Falcon during the airport battle.

campaignTags.claim: Rhodes wears advanced military mechanized armor suites.
War Machine armor provides supersonic powered flight.
Armor utilizes advanced Stark and military weapons technology.
Rhodes is a trained United States Air Force colonel and expert pilot.

unknowns: Performance limits of the Mark IV armor without military supply lines.

characters.summary: Operating as the Iron Patriot, James Rhodes wears a red, white, and blue repainted War Machine armor to serve as the official government mascot and heavy combatant.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to remote password override and security bypasses
characters.formDifferences: Changes the armor paint scheme to a red, white, and blue patriotic design commissioned by the US government, while retaining standard War Machine weapon systems.

sources.supports: Iron Patriot armor specifications, paint scheme, and usage in Iron Man 3.

notableResults.note: Fights modified Extremis combatants alongside Tony Stark.

unknowns: Any internal hardware upgrades compared to the standard Mark II/III War Machine armor.

characters.summary: Bucky Barnes fights as a ruthless assassin using peak human physical conditioning, extensive martial arts proficiency, firearms, tactical knives, and a vibranium-reinforced cybernetic left arm.
weaknesses: Psychological conditioning trigger words that can temporarily incapacitate or control him
limitations: Relies on standard military firearms and tactical equipment requiring ammunition

sources.supports: Bucky Barnes, Winter Soldier background, cybernetic arm, and combat skills.

feats.claim: Catches Captain America's vibranium shield mid-throw with his cybernetic arm.

notableResults.note: Fights Steve Rogers to a standstill on a highway bridge before intervention occurs.

campaignTags.claim: Bucky possesses a cybernetic left arm grafted onto his body.
Trained as a covert operative and assassin for the Soviet Union and Hydra.

unknowns: Complete extent of the super-soldier serum variants administered to him by Hydra.

characters.summary: Using the iconic shield and tactical expertise, Bucky Barnes adopts the mantle of Captain America to lead teams in combat with enhanced vibranium shielding and martial arts.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to being disarmed of the shield
characters.formDifferences: Wields Captain America's signature vibranium shield instead of relying solely on firearms and his cybernetic arm.

sources.supports: Bucky wielding Captain America's shield temporarily during Endgame.

notableResults.note: Participates in the final battle wielding the shield.

unknowns: Whether he formally accepted the permanent mantle of Captain America in the main timeline.

characters.summary: Cleansed of his Hydra programming in Wakanda, Bucky operates as the White Wolf, utilizing advanced Wakandan weaponry, a pristine vibranium arm, and tactical guerrilla combat.
weaknesses: None significantly noted beyond human vulnerability outside of armor
characters.formDifferences: Replaces his old Hydra cybernetic arm with a seamless Wakandan vibranium replacement and equips Wakandan military hardware.

sources.supports: Bucky Barnes' designation as the White Wolf and Wakandan gear in Infinity War.

notableResults.note: Fights in the Battle of Wakanda using advanced Wakandan firearms.

unknowns: Full capabilities of the Wakandan arm energy discharge functions.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe / Fox X-Men Universe
characters.summary: An aging, weary Logan whose healing factor has degraded, leaving him with chronic pain and physical scarring. He fights with brutal, desperate claw work and pragmatic lethality.
weaknesses: Degraded healing factor leading to slow recovery from major wounds
characters.formDifferences: Depicts Logan in advanced age with a malfunctioning healing factor, physical scars, and diminished stamina compared to his prime.

sources.supports: Logan character details, aging condition, degraded healing factor, and combat style in Logan (2017).

notableResults.note: Logan is fatally impaled by an enraged clone of himself (X-24) after his healing factor fails.

unknowns: Exact rate of healing factor decay over time.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe / Fox X-Men Universe
characters.summary: Feral and enraged, Logan in his Weapon X program state fights with absolute unbridled savagery after having his skeleton bonded with adamantium, possessing peak mutant regeneration and retracted claws.
weaknesses: Prone to blind berserker rage without tactical restraint
characters.formDifferences: Logan immediately following the Weapon X procedure, stripped of clothing, operating in a feral, memory-wiped state with maximum regeneration speed.

sources.supports: Weapon X procedure, adamantium bonding, and feral breakout in X-Men Origins: Wolverine.

notableResults.note: Escapes the facility by slaughtering numerous armed guards and tearing through walls.

unknowns: Full psychological recovery timeline following the memory wipe.
